data.name: Houd
data.gender_notes: Houd is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'h-d-d' meaning 'to help'. This name symbolizes providing support and assistance, both spiritually and materially. The name Houd carries the meaning “Help, Support” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Houd usually hope their child will grow to embody help, support and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Houd belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Help, Support.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Houd total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic history and literature, Hud, or Hood, is a prophet/messenger sent to the people of Ad (a specific tribe) to guide them towards righteousness and warn them of impending punishment for their disobedience towards Allah. This name has become synonymous with helping and supporting others, especially in a moral or spiritual sense, as seen in the story of Prophet Hud in the Quran.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Houd has significant spiritual importance in Islamic culture. It emphasizes the importance of helping and supporting others in their spiritual journeys, reminding us of the fundamental Islamic belief in the interconnectedness of humanity. It is also a reminder that as believers, we have a responsibility to guide and support our fellow beings on their path to Allah. This name fosters a sense of unity and compassion, inspiring us to be active agents of positive change in the world around us.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdisi, 'The Straight Path' (Al-Siraj Al-Munir), 12th century CE, the author describes Houd as a river that flows from the mountains of Yemen to the Red Sea, which is considered sacred in Islamic tradition. It is mentioned in the Hadith that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) performed the 'Wudu' (ablution) with water from the Houd river before setting out on the expedition of Tabuk.
historical_references.context: Islamic tradition, Hadith, Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), ablution, expedition of Tabuk

historical_references.reference: Al-Masudi, 'The Meadows of Gold' (Murūj al-Dhahab), 10th century CE, the author describes Houd as a river in Yemen that is considered one of the four major rivers in Islamic geography. It is also mentioned that King Herod the Great is believed to have obtained large quantities of gold from this river during his rule over Arabia.
historical_references.context: Islamic geography, King Herod the Great, gold

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Houd' has gained popularity in the modern tech industry due to its association with the legendary magician from Arabian folklore, who was known for his ability to escape from impossible situations. In the tech world, the name has been adopted by developers and organizations for their innovative projects related to technology innovation, particularly in the areas of artificial intelligence and science fiction. One of the most notable usage of 'Houd' can be seen in the form of chatbots and automated systems built using Microsoft's Azure Bot Service, Amazon Web Services Lambda, and Google Cloud Functions. These systems, named after the magician, are designed to escape the constraints of traditional systems and provide users with seamless and intelligent interactions, making them an essential part of modern technology trends.
